barbell_bench_press.summary: The classic chest builder: lower the bar to your chest and press it back up.
steps: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar. Plant your feet and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, unrack it and hold it over your shoulders.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, elbows about 45° from your torso.
Breathe out and press up and slightly back until the bar is over your shoulders again.
tips: Keep your hips on the bench and don't bounce the bar off your chest.
Stack your wrists over your elbows instead of letting them bend back.

incline_barbell_bench_press.summary: Pressing on a 30–45° bench shifts more work to the upper chest.
steps: Set the bench to 30–45°, lie back, retract your shoulder blades and plant your feet.
Unrack the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lower it to your upper chest just below the collarbones.
Press back up to straight arms without slamming your elbows.
tips: Too steep an angle turns it into a shoulder press.
Don't flare your elbows to 90°; keep them a bit closer to your body.

decline_bench_press.summary: A head-down bench press that emphasises the lower chest.
steps: Hook your legs under the pads and lie back on the decline bench.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack, ideally with a spotter.
Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press it back up along the same path.
tips: Use a spotter: racking and unracking in this position is awkward.
Never bring the bar toward your neck.

dumbbell_bench_press.summary: Dumbbells give a longer range of motion and even out side-to-side strength.
steps: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back and bring them over your chest.
Turn your palms forward, retract your shoulder blades, feet on the floor.
Lower the dumbbells beside your chest until you feel a stretch.
Press up, bringing them slightly together over your chest.
tips: Don't clank the dumbbells together at the top.
After the set, bring them back to your thighs rather than dropping them out wide.

incline_dumbbell_press.summary: Incline dumbbell press for the upper chest and front delts.
steps: Set the bench to 30–45° and lie back with the dumbbells over your shoulders.
Palms forward, shoulder blades retracted.
Lower the dumbbells to upper-chest level.
Press up and slightly in.
tips: Don't arch your lower back to turn it into a flat press.
Take 2–3 seconds on the way down.

dumbbell_fly.summary: Dumbbell flyes stretch and isolate the chest.
steps: Lie on a bench with the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep that angle.
Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a light stretch in your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back along the same arc, as if hugging a barrel.
tips: Don't bend and straighten your elbows; that makes it a press.
Go lighter than for presses: the shoulder is vulnerable at the bottom.

machine_chest_press.summary: A fixed path lets you load the chest safely without a spotter.
steps: Set the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest.
Keep your back on the pad and your shoulder blades together.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades on the pad at the end of the press.
Don't let the weight stack crash between reps.

smith_bench_press.summary: Bench pressing in a Smith machine: the bar runs on rails, so you can train without a spotter.
steps: Position the bench so the bar lands on your lower chest.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, retract your shoulder blades and unrack by rotating your wrists.
Lower the bar to your chest under control.
Press up and lock the hooks at the end of the set.
tips: Check the bench position before the first set; you can't adjust mid-rep.
The path is fixed, so don't push the bar toward your head.

pec_deck.summary: The pec deck isolates the chest with a guided fly.
steps: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Keep your back on the pad and hold the handles or press your forearms into the pads.
Bring your arms together in front of you, squeezing your chest.
Open slowly until you feel a light stretch.
tips: Don't let your arms travel far behind you; that loads the shoulders, not the chest.
Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

cable_crossover.summary: Cable flyes keep tension on the chest through the whole rep.
steps: Set the pulleys high, grab the handles and step forward.
Lean slightly forward with a soft bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands down and together in an arc in front of your hips.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
tips: Keep the elbow angle fixed; the movement comes from the shoulder.
Keep your torso still; don't rock.

push_up.summary: The bodyweight classic for chest, triceps and core.
steps: Get into a high plank with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep a straight line from head to heels; brace your glutes and abs.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, elbows about 45° from your torso.
Push back up to straight arms.
tips: Don't let your hips sag or pike up.
Too hard? Do them from your knees or with your hands on a bench.

chest_dips.summary: Dips with a forward lean target the lower chest.
steps: Support yourself on the parallel bars with straight arms.
Lean your torso forward and let your elbows flare slightly.
Lower until your elbows reach about 90° or you feel a chest stretch.
Press yourself back up, keeping the lean.
tips: Don't go too deep if your shoulders hurt.
Staying upright shifts the work to your triceps.

pull_up.summary: Wide-grip pull-ups: the go-to exercise for a wider back.
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulders down and your shoulder blades together.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, driving your elbows down.
Lower under control to straight arms.
tips: Don't swing or kick your legs.
Not strong enough yet? Start with the assisted machine or a band.

assisted_pull_up.summary: Assisted pull-ups: the counterweight takes part of your body weight.
steps: Set the counterweight: more weight means more help.
Kneel on the platform and grab the handles wider than your shoulders.
Pull until your chin is above the handles, driving your elbows down.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Progress here means using less counterweight.
Keep your chest up; don't hunch.

lat_pulldown.summary: Pulling the bar to your chest builds the lats.
steps: Sit with your thighs under the pads and grip the bar wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, bringing your shoulder blades together and your elbows down.
Let the bar rise smoothly until your arms are straight.
tips: Don't pull behind your neck or lean far back.
Pull with your elbows, not your hands.

close_grip_lat_pulldown.summary: A close neutral grip gives the lats a longer range of motion.
steps: Attach a V-handle, sit down and lock your legs in.
Hold the handle with a neutral grip and straight arms.
Pull it to your upper chest, elbows down and close to your sides.
Return up, letting your shoulder blades spread.
tips: Keep your torso almost still with a slight lean back.
Don't round your back at the bottom.

straight_arm_pulldown.summary: A straight-arm cable pullover isolates the lats.
steps: Stand facing a high pulley and hold a bar or rope with straight arms.
Hinge slightly forward with a flat back.
Sweep your arms down to your thighs without bending your elbows.
Return your arms smoothly to head height.
tips: Soft elbows are fine, but the angle must not change.
Don't help with your torso.

seated_cable_row.summary: Seated cable rows work the middle of the back.
steps: Sit, brace your feet and hold the V-handle with straight arms and a flat back.
Pull the handle to your stomach, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly with your shoulder blades squeezed.
Straighten your arms slowly without rounding your back.
tips: Don't rock your torso back and forth.
Keep your shoulders down.

barbell_row.summary: Bent-over barbell rows build a thick, strong back.
steps: Grip the bar at shoulder width with a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge forward with a flat back to about 45° or lower.
Pull the bar to your lower stomach, driving your elbows back.
Lower under control to straight arms.
tips: Never round your lower back; it's the main risk here.
Don't jerk your torso upright on every rep.

t_bar_row.summary: T-bar rows for a thicker mid-back.
steps: Straddle the bar with feet shoulder-width apart and grab the handle.
Hinge forward with a flat back and soft knees.
Pull the weight to your stomach, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control.
tips: Keep your lower back neutral.
Don't use your legs or momentum.

dumbbell_row.summary: One-arm dumbbell rows with support on a bench.
steps: Place one knee and hand on the bench, back flat and parallel to the floor.
Hold the dumbbell in your free hand with a straight arm.
Row it to your hip, elbow close to your body.
Lower to a full stretch.
tips: Don't twist your torso to heave the weight up.
Drive your elbow back, not up.

machine_row.summary: A chest-supported machine row trains the back without loading the lower back.
steps: Set the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height.
Press your chest into the pad and grab the handles.
Pull the handles toward you, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly to straight arms.
tips: Keep your chest on the pad.
Don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears.

deadlift.summary: Lifting a barbell off the floor works the entire back of the body.
steps: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar just outside your knees, back flat, chest up.
Push the floor away with your legs, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Stand up fully, then lower the bar along the same path.
tips: Never round your back: less weight with perfect form is better.
Keep the bar close and don't lean back at the top.

back_extension.summary: Back extensions strengthen the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Set the pad under your hips, not your stomach.
Cross your arms over your chest, body in a straight line.
Hinge down with a flat back.
Raise your torso back into line with your legs.
tips: Don't hyperextend past a straight line.
Hold a weight only once 15+ reps feel easy.

overhead_press.summary: The standing barbell press builds the shoulders and a stable core.
steps: Unrack the bar at collarbone height with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Feet hip-width apart; brace your glutes and abs.
Press the bar up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Lock out overhead, then lower slowly to your collarbones.
tips: Don't arch your lower back; keep your torso rigid.
Don't use your legs unless you mean to push press.

seated_dumbbell_press.summary: Seated dumbbell press for the front and side delts.
steps: Sit on an upright bench with the dumbbells at shoulder height.
Palms forward, back against the pad.
Press the dumbbells up, bringing them slightly together overhead.
Lower to ear level or slightly below.
tips: Keep your back on the pad.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body, not straight out to the sides.

machine_shoulder_press.summary: Machine shoulder press: a safe path with no balancing.
steps: Set the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Keep your back on the pad and grab the handles.
Press up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly to shoulder level.
tips: Don't snap your elbows into lockout.
Keep your shoulders down.

lateral_raise.summary: Dumbbell lateral raises target the side delts.
steps: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your thighs and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Keep your little finger slightly higher, as if pouring from a jug.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't swing or use your torso.
No need to go above shoulder height; that brings in the traps.

cable_lateral_raise.summary: A low-pulley lateral raise keeps tension on the delt through the whole range.
steps: Stand side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in your far hand.
Start with the hand in front of your hips, elbow slightly bent.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Return slowly.
tips: Keep your torso still; hold the frame with your free hand.
Use a light weight and control.

front_raise.summary: Dumbbell front raises for the front delts.
steps: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Raise one or both dumbbells with straight arms to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't lean back to lift the weight.
Front delts already work hard in presses, so a few sets are enough.

rear_delt_fly.summary: Bent-over dumbbell raises for the rear delts.
steps: Sit on the end of a bench and lean forward, chest toward your thighs, dumbbells under your legs.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows, palms facing each other.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't squeeze your shoulder blades hard; that turns it into a back exercise.
Use a light weight and a short, controlled motion.

reverse_pec_deck.summary: Reverse flyes on the pec deck for the rear delts.
steps: Sit facing the pad with the handles at shoulder height.
Grab them with straight arms and a slight bend in your elbows.
Open your arms back until they line up with your torso.
Return forward slowly.
tips: Don't throw your head and torso back.
Keep your shoulders down.

face_pull.summary: Pulling a rope to your face builds the rear delts and healthy shoulders.
steps: Set the pulley at face height and take the rope with an overhand grip.
Step back with straight arms.
Pull the rope toward your face, spreading the ends and lifting your elbows high and wide.
Straighten your arms slowly.
tips: Finish with your hands behind your elbows, as if flexing your biceps.
Don't lean back.

upright_row.summary: Barbell upright rows for the delts and traps.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width grip.
Pull the bar up along your body to just below your chest, elbows above your hands.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't pull above shoulder level if your shoulder feels pinched.
A wider grip is easier on the shoulder joint.

barbell_curl.summary: Standing barbell curls for the biceps.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
tips: Don't swing your torso or let your elbows drift forward.
Lower more slowly than you lift.

dumbbell_curl.summary: Dumbbell curls train each arm on its own.
steps: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing you.
Curl, turning your palm up as you lift.
Bring the dumbbell to your shoulder.
Lower slowly, turning the palm back toward you.
tips: Keep your elbows by your sides.
Don't help by swinging your shoulder forward.

hammer_curl.summary: Hammer curls with a neutral grip for the biceps and brachialis.
steps: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
Curl without changing your grip.
Bring the dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
tips: Keep your wrists straight.
Alternating arms is fine, but don't swing.

preacher_curl.summary: Preacher curls stop your body from helping the biceps.
steps: Sit and rest the backs of your upper arms on the pad.
Hold the bar with an underhand grip, arms almost straight.
Curl until your forearms are vertical.
Lower slowly without snapping into a straight arm.
tips: The biceps are vulnerable at the bottom, so no jerking.
Keep your elbows on the pad.

cable_curl.summary: Low-pulley cable curls keep constant tension on the biceps.
steps: Stand facing a low pulley and hold a straight or EZ bar underhand.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Return slowly.
tips: Stand close so the cable runs vertically.
Keep your torso still.

machine_curl.summary: Machine curls give the biceps a stable path.
steps: Set the seat so your elbows rest on the pad in line with the machine's pivot.
Grab the handles underhand.
Curl all the way up.
Return slowly.
tips: Line your elbows up with the pivot.
Keep your upper arms on the pad.

steps: Stand facing a high pulley and grab a straight bar overhand.
Pin your elbows to your sides, forearms parallel to the floor.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly to 90°.
tips: Your elbows shouldn't move forward or back.
Don't lean over the bar.

rope_pushdown.summary: Rope pushdowns: spread the ends at the bottom for a full squeeze.
steps: Hold the rope with a neutral grip, elbows by your sides.
Push down to straighten your arms.
At the bottom, pull the rope ends apart.
Return slowly.
tips: Keep your elbows still.
Don't lean forward to help.

skull_crusher.summary: Lying triceps extensions with an EZ bar.
steps: Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar over your chest with straight arms.
Tilt your arms slightly back toward your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar to your forehead or just behind your head.
Extend your arms without moving your upper arms.
tips: Don't let your elbows flare out.
Use a moderate weight: elbows don't like jerks.

overhead_triceps_extension.summary: Overhead dumbbell extensions stretch the long head of the triceps.
steps: Hold one dumbbell with both hands under the top plate and lift it overhead.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back up.
tips: Brace your abs so your lower back doesn't arch.
Don't let your elbows flare wide.

close_grip_bench_press.summary: Close-grip bench press: a heavy compound for the triceps.
steps: Lie on the bench and grip the bar at shoulder width.
Unrack with your shoulder blades retracted.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows close to your body.
Press back up.
tips: Too narrow a grip strains the wrists.
Don't flare your elbows.

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands next to your hips.
Slide off the bench with your legs out in front.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips until your elbows reach 90°.
Straighten your arms to come back up.
tips: Keep your back close to the bench.
Don't go too deep if your shoulders hurt.

steps: Set the seat so your elbows rest on the pad in line with the pivot.
Grab the handles with your elbows bent.
Extend your arms fully.
Return slowly.
tips: Keep your upper arms still.
Don't let the stack crash.

back_squat.summary: The barbell back squat: the main exercise for legs and glutes.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper traps, unrack, feet slightly wider than your shoulders, toes turned out a little.
Breathe in, brace and start by sending your hips back and your knees out over your toes.
Squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower, back flat.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot; breathe out near the top.
tips: Don't let your knees cave in.
Keep your heels down with your weight over mid-foot.

front_squat.summary: With the bar on your front delts, the front squat loads the quads more.
steps: Rest the bar on your front delts near your neck, elbows high and forward.
Feet shoulder-width apart, torso upright.
Squat down, keeping your elbows high and chest open.
Stand up without tipping forward.
tips: If your elbows drop, the bar rolls forward.
Your shoulders hold the bar; your fingers only steady it.

sumo_deadlift.summary: A wide-stance deadlift: shorter range, more glutes and adductors.
steps: Take a wide stance with your toes out and the bar over mid-foot.
Grip the bar between your knees with a narrow grip, back flat.
Push your knees out and stand up, keeping the bar against your body.
Lock out fully, then lower under control.
tips: Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Don't let your hips rise faster than your shoulders.

romanian_deadlift.summary: The Romanian deadlift: a flat-back hinge that stretches the hamstrings.
steps: Stand holding the bar, feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back, sliding the bar down your thighs.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand up.
tips: Keep your back flat the whole time; never round your lower back.
Your knee angle barely changes: it's not a squat.

leg_press.summary: The leg press loads quads and glutes without compressing the spine.
steps: Sit with your lower back against the pad and feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Release the safeties and lower the platform until your knees reach about 90°.
Press the platform away through your whole foot.
Don't lock your knees at the top.
tips: Keep your hips on the seat at the bottom.
Knees should track over your toes.

hack_squat.summary: The machine hack squat emphasises the quads.
steps: Step into the machine with your back and shoulders on the pads, feet on the platform.
Release the safeties and lower as deep as you can without your hips coming off.
Drive up through your whole foot.
Don't lock your knees at the top.
tips: Feet lower works the quads more; higher works the glutes more.
Keep your back on the pad.

smith_squat.summary: Squatting in a Smith machine: a fixed path you can train without a spotter.
steps: Step under the bar, rest it on your traps, feet slightly forward.
Unrack by rotating your wrists.
Squat to parallel with a flat back.
Stand up and lock the hooks at the end of the set.
tips: Place your feet slightly in front of you, or your knees travel far forward.
Set the safety stops before your first set.

steps: Adjust the back pad so your knees line up with the pivot and the roller sits above your ankles.
Hold the handles and keep your hips down.
Extend your legs fully and pause.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't kick the weight up.
Keep your hips on the seat.

lying_leg_curl.summary: Lying leg curls for the hamstrings.
steps: Lie face down with your knees just past the edge and the roller above your heels.
Hold the handles and keep your hips down.
Curl the roller toward your glutes.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
tips: Don't let your hips lift off the bench.
Control the way down; don't drop the weight.

seated_leg_curl.summary: Seated leg curls work the hamstrings in a lengthened position.
steps: Sit with your knees at the pivot, the roller above your heels and the thigh pad locked down.
Hold the handles with your back against the pad.
Curl your legs as far as you can.
Return slowly.
tips: Leaning slightly forward increases the stretch.
No jerking.

hip_adduction.summary: The adductor machine works your inner thighs.
steps: Sit with the pads against the inside of your knees.
Set a comfortable starting width.
Squeeze your legs together and pause.
Open slowly.
tips: Keep your back against the pad.
Don't open wider than your flexibility allows.

walking_lunge.summary: Dumbbell walking lunges for legs and glutes.
steps: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90°.
Push off the front foot and step into the next lunge.
Alternate legs with an upright torso.
tips: Your back knee should almost touch the floor.
Don't let your front knee cave in.

bulgarian_split_squat.summary: Bulgarian split squats: rear foot on a bench, heavy work for one leg and glute.
steps: Stand with your back to a bench and rest the top of your rear foot on it.
Place your front foot a big step ahead.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Stand up with your front leg.
tips: A slight forward lean hits the glutes more; upright hits the quads more.
Start without weight to find your balance.

goblet_squat.summary: Holding a dumbbell at your chest helps you squat with a flat back.
steps: Hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest with both hands.
Feet slightly wider than your shoulders, toes turned out a little.
Squat deep with your elbows inside your knees.
Stand up through your whole foot.
tips: Chest up, dumbbell close to your body.
A great way to learn the squat pattern.

step_up.summary: Dumbbell step-ups for legs and glutes.
steps: Stand in front of a bench or box with dumbbells in your hands.
Place one whole foot on the bench.
Step up by driving through the top leg.
Step down slowly with the same leg, then switch.
tips: Don't push off with the bottom leg.
Keep your knee over your foot.

hip_thrust.summary: The barbell hip thrust: the best exercise for the glutes.
steps: Sit on the floor with your shoulder blades on a bench and the bar over your hips, with a pad.
Feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent.
Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and lower slowly.
tips: Don't arch your lower back at the top.
Shins should be vertical at the top.

glute_bridge.summary: The floor glute bridge: a basic glute exercise.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet near your glutes.
Arms by your sides.
Lift your hips by squeezing your glutes.
Pause and lower slowly.
tips: Push through your heels, not your toes.
Don't overarch your lower back.

hip_abduction.summary: The abductor machine works the outer thighs and glutes.
steps: Sit with the pads against the outside of your knees.
Legs together, back against the pad.
Push your legs apart and pause.
Bring them back together slowly.
tips: Leaning forward puts more work on the glutes.
Don't let the pads slam together.

steps: Step into the machine, support yourself on your chest or hands, foot on the platform.
Keep your torso still.
Push your leg back, squeezing the glute.
Return slowly.
tips: Don't arch your lower back to kick further.
Move from the hip.

cable_kickback.summary: Cable glute kickbacks from a low pulley.
steps: Strap the cuff around your ankle and face the pulley.
Hold the frame and lean slightly forward.
Kick your leg back and slightly up.
Return slowly.
tips: Don't swing your torso.
Keep a soft bend in the standing leg.

steps: Step into the machine with your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the edge.
Lower your heels into a stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause and lower slowly.
tips: Knees straight but not locked.
Full range of motion matters more than the weight.

seated_calf_raise.summary: Seated calf raises target the soleus.
steps: Sit with the pad on your thighs near your knees and the balls of your feet on the edge.
Release the lock and lower your heels into a stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't bounce at the bottom.
A pause at the top makes it more effective.

leg_press_calf_raise.summary: Calf raises on the leg press machine.
steps: Sit in the machine with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Legs straight; keep the safety stops engaged if the machine allows.
Push the platform away with your toes.
Return slowly into a calf stretch.
tips: Go slowly so your feet don't slip off.
Don't bend your knees to help.

plank.summary: The plank: a static hold for the core.
steps: Get onto your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back onto your toes.
Keep a straight line from head to heels with glutes and abs braced.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
tips: Don't let your hips sag or pike up.
Log the time in seconds in the reps field.

crunch.summary: Floor crunches for the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet on the floor.
Hands by your temples or crossed on your chest.
Curl your torso up until your shoulder blades leave the floor.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't pull your head with your hands.
Your lower back stays on the floor.

hanging_leg_raise.summary: Hanging leg raises for the lower abs.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Brace your abs to stop swinging.
Raise your legs to hip height or higher, curling your pelvis up.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't swing: use your muscles, not momentum.
Too hard with straight legs? Raise bent knees.

steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lean back to about 45°.
Hold your hands or a weight in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso from side to side.
Keep a controlled pace.
tips: Keep your back straight; don't slump.
Rotate your torso, not just your arms.

cable_crunch.summary: Kneeling rope crunches on a high pulley.
steps: Kneel in front of a high pulley and hold the rope beside your head.
Keep your hips still.
Crunch down, bringing your elbows toward your thighs.
Return up slowly.
tips: Don't sit back onto your heels: the movement comes from your spine.
Don't pull with your arms.

steps: Adjust the seat, hold the handles and hook your feet under the rollers.
Keep your back against the pad.
Crunch forward, bringing your chest toward your hips.
Return slowly.
tips: Don't pull with your arms.
Breathe out as you crunch.

ab_wheel.summary: Ab wheel rollouts from your knees build a strong core.
steps: Kneel with the wheel on the floor under your shoulders.
Brace your abs and glutes.
Roll the wheel forward slowly as far as you can with a flat back.
Pull back using your abs.
tips: Don't let your lower back sag.
Increase the range gradually.

kettlebell_swing.summary: Kettlebell swings: an explosive hip drive for glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Stand slightly wider than your shoulders with the kettlebell on the floor in front.
Hinge with a flat back, grab the bell and hike it between your legs.
Snap your hips forward so the bell floats up to chest height.
Let it swing back between your legs and repeat.
tips: Your arms just hold the bell; the power comes from your hips.
It's a hinge, not a squat.

farmers_walk.summary: Walking with heavy dumbbells trains grip, traps and core.
steps: Pick up heavy dumbbells in both hands.
Stand tall, shoulders down, shoulder blades back.
Walk with short steps for a set distance or time.
Set the dumbbells down with a flat back.
tips: Don't slouch or sway.
Log the weight of one dumbbell.

clean_and_press.summary: Clean and press: an explosive full-body lift.
steps: Stand at the bar, feet hip-width apart, grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lift the bar off the floor, extend your hips explosively and pull the bar up.
Drop under the bar and catch it on your front delts.
Stand up and press it overhead, then lower to your shoulders and to the floor.
tips: Learn it with a light weight: technique matters more than load.
Keep a flat back at every stage.

burpee.summary: Burpees: squat, plank and jump in one movement.
steps: Stand tall, squat and put your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a plank (add a push-up if you like).
Jump your feet back to your hands.
Jump up with your arms overhead.
tips: Keep your hips level in the plank.
Land softly on bent knees.
